title: Ruby review conventions
summary: Read-only review guidance for Ruby and Rails: mass assignment, unsafe metaprogramming, query patterns and test isolation. Ruby implementation is not delegated.

provenance.notes: Review-only. Ruby is deliberately out of scope for delegated implementation, and no worker receives this skill.

outputs.name: findings
outputs.description: Security, correctness and performance findings with line references.

workflow.step: Find places where request parameters reach models or queries and check strong parameters, validation and SQL interpolation.
workflow.check: No raw parameter reaches a query or a mass assignment.

workflow.step: Find dynamic dispatch and eval-like calls (send, public_send, constantize, instance_eval) fed by external values.
workflow.check: External strings never choose a method or a constant unchecked.

workflow.step: Look for N+1 queries and missing indexes in loops over associations.
workflow.check: Loops that issue a query per row are flagged.

workflow.step: Check Gemfile changes for new gems, unpinned versions and git sources.
Check tests isolate state and cover failure paths rather than only the happy path.

constraints: Read-only analysis; Ruby implementation is out of scope.
Do not run the application or its console.

examples.title: send with params
examples.guidance: Report as critical: external input chooses the method. Replace with an explicit allow-list.

verification: Every finding cites a file and line.

task.text: Review the rails controller for mass assignment and a send call on activerecord.
The rspec suite shows an n+1 query in the gem.
Write an rspec for the rails model.
